NKJV.1: ‘When anyone offers a grain offering to the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour. And he shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it.
NKJV.2: He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests, one of whom shall take from it his handful of fine flour and oil with all the frankincense. And the priest shall burn it as a memorial on the altar, an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the LORD.
NKJV.3: The rest of the grain offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is most holy of the offerings to the LORD made by fire.
NKJV.4: ‘And if you bring as an offering a grain offering baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
NKJV.5: But if your offering is a grain offering baked in a pan, it shall be of fine flour, unleavened, mixed with oil.
NKJV.6: You shall break it in pieces and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
NKJV.7: ‘If your offering is a grain offering baked in a covered pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
NKJV.8: You shall bring the grain offering that is made of these things to the LORD. And when it is presented to the priest, he shall bring it to the altar.
NKJV.9: Then the priest shall take from the grain offering a memorial portion, and burn it on the altar. It is an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the LORD.
NKJV.10: And what is left of the grain offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is most holy of the offerings to the LORD made by fire.
NKJV.11: ‘No grain offering which you bring to the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you shall burn no leaven nor any honey in any offering to the LORD made by fire.
NKJV.12: As for the offering of the firstfruits, you shall offer them to the LORD, but they shall not be burned on the altar for a sweet aroma.
NKJV.13: And every offering of your grain offering you shall season with salt; you shall not allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be lacking from your grain offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
NKJV.14: ‘If you offer a grain offering of your firstfruits to the LORD, you shall offer for the grain offering of your firstfruits green heads of grain roasted on the fire, grain beaten from full heads.
NKJV.15: And you shall put oil on it, and lay frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
NKJV.16: Then the priest shall burn the memorial portion: part of its beaten grain and part of its oil, with all the frankincense, as an offering made by fire to the LORD.

NASB.1: 'Now when anyone presents a grain offering as an offering to the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour, and he shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.
NASB.2: 'He shall then bring it to Aaron's sons the priests; and shall take from it his handful of its fine flour and of its oil with all of its frankincense. And the priest shall offer [it] up in smoke [as] its memorial portion on the altar, an offering by fire of a soothing aroma to the LORD.
NASB.3: 'The remainder of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons: a thing most holy, of the offerings to the LORD by fire.
NASB.4: 'Now when you bring an offering of a grain offering baked in an oven, [it shall be] unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
NASB.5: 'If your offering is a grain offering [made] on the griddle, [it shall be] of fine flour, unleavened, mixed with oil;
NASB.6: you shall break it into bits and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
NASB.7: 'Now if your offering is a grain offering [made] in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
NASB.8: 'When you bring in the grain offering which is made of these things to the LORD, it shall be presented to the priest and he shall bring it to the altar.
NASB.9: 'The priest then shall take up from the grain offering its memorial portion, and shall offer [it] up in smoke on the altar [as] an offering by fire of a soothing aroma to the LORD.
NASB.10: 'The remainder of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons: a thing most holy of the offerings to the LORD by fire.
NASB.11: 'No grain offering, which you bring to the LORD, shall be made with leaven, for you shall not offer up in smoke any leaven or any honey as an offering by fire to the LORD.
NASB.12: 'As an offering of first fruits you shall bring them to the LORD, but they shall not ascend for a soothing aroma on the altar.
NASB.13: 'Every grain offering of yours, moreover, you shall season with salt, so that the salt of the covenant of your God shall not be lacking from your grain offering; with all your offerings you shall offer salt.
NASB.14: 'Also if you bring a grain offering of early ripened things to the LORD, you shall bring fresh heads of grain roasted in the fire, grits of new growth, for the grain offering of your early ripened things.
NASB.15: 'You shall then put oil on it and lay incense on it; it is a grain offering.
NASB.16: 'The priest shall offer up in smoke its memorial portion, part of its grits and its oil with all its incense as an offering by fire to the LORD.

ESV.1: “When anyone brings a grain offering as an offering to the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour. He shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it
ESV.2: and bring it to Aaron's sons the priests. And he shall take from it a handful of the fine flour and oil, with all of its frankincense, and the priest shall burn this as its memorial portion on the altar, a food offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
ESV.3: But the rest of the grain offering shall be for Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the LORD's food offerings.
ESV.4: “When you bring a grain offering baked in the oven as an offering, it shall be unleavened loaves of fine flour mixed with oil or unleavened wafers smeared with oil.
ESV.5: And if your offering is a grain offering baked on a griddle, it shall be of fine flour unleavened, mixed with oil.
ESV.6: You shall break it in pieces and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
ESV.7: And if your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
ESV.8: And you shall bring the grain offering that is made of these things to the LORD, and when it is presented to the priest, he shall bring it to the altar.
ESV.9: And the priest shall take from the grain offering its memorial portion and burn this on the altar, a food offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
ESV.10: But the rest of the grain offering shall be for Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the LORD's food offerings.
ESV.11: “No grain offering that you bring to the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you shall burn no leaven nor any honey as a food offering to the LORD.
ESV.12: As an offering of firstfruits you may bring them to the LORD, but they shall not be offered on the altar for a pleasing aroma.
ESV.13: You shall season all your grain offerings with salt. You shall not let the salt of the covenant with your God be missing from your grain offering; with all your offerings you shall offer salt.
ESV.14: “If you offer a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you shall offer for the grain offering of your firstfruits fresh ears, roasted with fire, crushed new grain.
ESV.15: And you shall put oil on it and lay frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
ESV.16: And the priest shall burn as its memorial portion some of the crushed grain and some of the oil with all of its frankincense; it is a food offering to the LORD.

NLT.1: “When you present grain as an offering to the LORD, the offering must consist of choice flour. You are to pour olive oil on it, sprinkle it with frankincense,
NLT.2: and bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. The priest will scoop out a handful of the flour moistened with oil, together with all the frankincense, and burn this representative portion on the altar. It is a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
NLT.3: The rest of the grain offering will then be given to Aaron and his sons. This offering will be considered a most holy part of the special gifts presented to the LORD.
NLT.4: “If your offering is a grain offering baked in an oven, it must be made of choice flour, but without any yeast. It may be presented in the form of thin cakes mixed with olive oil or wafers spread with olive oil.
NLT.5: If your grain offering is cooked on a griddle, it must be made of choice flour mixed with olive oil but without any yeast.
NLT.6: Break it in pieces and pour olive oil on it; it is a grain offering.
NLT.7: If your grain offering is prepared in a pan, it must be made of choice flour and olive oil.
NLT.8: “No matter how a grain offering for the LORD has been prepared, bring it to the priest, who will present it at the altar.
NLT.9: The priest will take a representative portion of the grain offering and burn it on the altar. It is a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
NLT.10: The rest of the grain offering will then be given to Aaron and his sons as their food. This offering will be considered a most holy part of the special gifts presented to the LORD.
NLT.11: “Do not use yeast in preparing any of the grain offerings you present to the LORD, because no yeast or honey may be burned as a special gift presented to the LORD.
NLT.12: You may add yeast and honey to an offering of the first crops of your harvest, but these must never be offered on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
NLT.13: Season all your grain offerings with salt to remind you of God’s eternal covenant. Never forget to add salt to your grain offerings.
NLT.14: “If you present a grain offering to the LORD from the first portion of your harvest, bring fresh grain that is coarsely ground and roasted on a fire.
NLT.15: Put olive oil on this grain offering, and sprinkle it with frankincense.
NLT.16: The priest will take a representative portion of the grain moistened with oil, together with all the frankincense, and burn it as a special gift presented to the LORD.

WEB.1: “‘When anyone offers an offering of a meal offering to Yahweh, his offering shall be of fine flour. He shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it.
WEB.2: He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests; and he shall take his handful of its fine flour, and of its oil, with all its frankincense; and the priest shall burn its memorial on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahweh.
WEB.3: That which is left of the meal offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a most holy thing of the offerings of Yahweh made by fire.
WEB.4: “‘When you offer an offering of a meal offering baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
WEB.5: If your offering is a meal offering of the griddle, it shall be of unleavened fine flour, mixed with oil.
WEB.6: You shall cut it in pieces, and pour oil on it. It is a meal offering.
WEB.7: If your offering is a meal offering of the pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
WEB.8: You shall bring the meal offering that is made of these things to Yahweh: and it shall be presented to the priest, and he shall bring it to the altar.
WEB.9: The priest shall take from the meal offering its memorial, and shall burn it on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahweh.
WEB.10: That which is left of the meal offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a thing most holy of the offerings of Yahweh made by fire.
WEB.11: “‘No meal offering, which you shall offer to Yahweh, shall be made with yeast; for you shall burn no yeast, nor any honey, as an offering made by fire to Yahweh.
WEB.12: As an offering of first fruits you shall offer them to Yahweh: but they shall not rise up for a pleasant aroma on the altar.
WEB.13: Every offering of your meal offering you shall season with salt. You shall not allow the salt of the covenant of your God  to be lacking from your meal offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
WEB.14: “‘If you offer a meal offering of first fruits to Yahweh, you shall offer for the meal offering of your first fruits grain in the ear parched with fire, bruised grain of the fresh ear.
WEB.15: You shall put oil on it, and lay frankincense on it: it is a meal offering.
WEB.16: The priest shall burn as its memorial, part of its bruised grain, and part of its oil, along with all its frankincense: it is an offering made by fire to Yahweh.

CSB17.1: “When anyone presents a grain offering <sup>ⓜ</sup> as an offering to the LORD, it is to consist of fine flour. <sup>ⓝ</sup> He is to pour olive oil <sup>ⓐ</sup> on it, put frankincense on it, <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.2: and bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests. The priest will take a handful of fine flour and oil from it, along with all its frankincense, and will burn this memorial portion <sup>ⓒ</sup> of it on the altar, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
CSB17.3: But the rest of the grain offering will belong to Aaron and his sons; it is the holiest part <sup>ⓓ</sup> of the fire offerings to the LORD.
CSB17.4: “When you present a grain offering baked in an oven, it is to be made of fine flour, either unleavened cakes <sup>ⓔ</sup> mixed with oil or unleavened wafers <sup>ⓕ</sup> coated with oil.
CSB17.5: If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, <sup>ⓖ</sup> it is to be unleavened bread <sup>ⓗ</sup> made of fine flour mixed with oil.
CSB17.6: Break it into pieces and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
CSB17.7: If your offering is a grain offering prepared in a pan, <sup>ⓘ</sup> it is to be made of fine flour with oil.
CSB17.8: When you bring to the LORD the grain offering made in any of these ways, it is to be presented to the priest, and he will take it to the altar.
CSB17.9: The priest will remove the memorial portion <sup>[1]</sup> from the grain offering and burn it on the altar, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
CSB17.10: But the rest of the grain offering will belong to Aaron and his sons; <sup>ⓙ</sup> it is the holiest part of the fire offerings to the LORD.
CSB17.11: “No grain offering that you present to the LORD is to be made with yeast, for you are not to burn <sup>[2]</sup> any yeast <sup>ⓚ</sup> or honey <sup>ⓛ</sup> as a fire offering to the LORD.
CSB17.12: You may present them to the LORD as an offering of firstfruits, <sup>ⓜ</sup> but they are not to be offered on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
CSB17.13: You are to season each of your grain offerings with salt; you must not omit from your grain offering the salt of the covenant <sup>ⓝ</sup> with your God. You are to present salt with each of your offerings.
CSB17.14: “If you present a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you are to present fresh heads of grain, crushed kernels, roasted on the fire, for your grain offering of firstfruits.
CSB17.15: You are to put oil and frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
CSB17.16: The priest will then burn some of its crushed kernels and oil with all its frankincense as a fire offering to the LORD.

AMP.1: 'When anyone presents a grain offering to the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour, and he shall pour [olive] oil over it and put frankincense on it.
AMP.2: He shall bring it to Aaron's sons the priests. Out of it he shall take a handful of the fine flour and oil, with all of its frankincense, and the priest shall offer this up in smoke on the altar [of burnt offering] as the memorial portion of it. It is an offering by fire, a sweet and soothing aroma to the LORD.
AMP.3: What is left of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the offerings to the LORD by fire.
AMP.4: 'When you bring an offering of grain baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
AMP.5: If your offering is grain baked on a griddle, it shall be of fine unleavened flour, mixed with oil.
AMP.6: You are to break it into pieces, and you shall pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
AMP.7: Now if your offering is grain cooked in a lidded pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
AMP.8: When you bring the grain offering that is made of these things to the LORD, it shall be presented to the priest, and he shall bring it to the altar [of burnt offering].
AMP.9: The priest shall take from the grain offering its memorial portion and offer it up in smoke on the altar. It is an offering by fire, a sweet and soothing aroma to the LORD.
AMP.10: What is left of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the offerings to the LORD by fire.
AMP.11: 'No grain offering that you bring to the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you shall not offer up in smoke any leaven [which symbolizes the spread of sin] or any honey [which, like leaven, is subject to fermentation] in any offering by fire to the LORD.
AMP.12: As an offering of first fruits you may offer them [leaven and honey] to the LORD, but they shall not go up [in smoke] on the altar as a sweet and soothing aroma.
AMP.13: You shall season every grain offering with salt so that the salt (preservation) of the covenant of your God will not be missing from your grain offering. You shall offer salt with all your offerings.
AMP.14: 'If you bring a grain offering of early ripened things to the LORD, you shall bring fresh heads of grain roasted in the fire, crushed grain of new growth, for the grain offering of your early ripened things.
AMP.15: You shall put oil on it and lay incense on it; it is a grain offering.
AMP.16: The priest shall offer up in smoke its memorial portion, part of the crushed grain and part of its oil with all its incense; it is an offering by fire to the LORD.

NIV.1:
The Grain Offering
“‘When someone brings a grain offering to the Lord, his offering is to be of fine flour. He is to pour oil on it, put incense on it
NIV.2: and take it to Aaron’s sons the priests. The priest shall take a handful of the fine flour and oil, together with all the incense, and burn this as a memorial portion on the altar, an offering made by fire, an aroma pleasing to the Lord.
NIV.3: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the offerings made to the Lord by fire.
NIV.4: “‘If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it is to consist of fine flour: cakes made without yeast and mixed with oil, or wafers made without yeast and spread with oil.
NIV.5: If your grain offering is prepared on a griddle, it is to be made of fine flour mixed with oil, and without yeast.
NIV.6: Crumble it and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
NIV.7: If your grain offering is cooked in a pan, it is to be made of fine flour and oil.
NIV.8: Bring the grain offering made of these things to the Lord; present it to the priest, who shall take it to the altar.
NIV.9: He shall take out the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as an offering made by fire, an aroma pleasing to the Lord.
NIV.10: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the offerings made to the Lord by fire.
NIV.11: “‘Every grain offering you bring to the Lord must be made without yeast, for you are not to burn any yeast or honey in an offering made to the Lord by fire.
NIV.12: You may bring them to the Lord as an offering of the firstfruits, but they are not to be offered on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
NIV.13: Season all your grain offerings with salt. Do not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offerings; add salt to all your offerings.
NIV.14: “‘If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the Lord, offer crushed heads of new grain roasted in the fire.
NIV.15: Put oil and incense on it; it is a grain offering.
NIV.16: The priest shall burn the memorial portion of the crushed grain and the oil, together with all the incense, as an offering made to the Lord by fire.

MSG.9: break off a memorial piece from the Grain-Offering, and burn it on the Altar: a Fire-Gift, a pleasing fragrance to God.

NRSVCE.5: If your offering is grain prepared on a griddle, it shall be of choice flour mixed with oil, unleavened;
NRSVCE.6: break it in pieces, and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
NRSVCE.7: If your offering is grain prepared in a pan, it shall be made of choice flour in oil.
NRSVCE.8: You shall bring to the LORD the grain offering that is prepared in any of these ways; and when it is presented to the priest, he shall take it to the altar.
NRSVCE.9: The priest shall remove from the grain offering its token portion and turn this into smoke on the altar, an offering by fire of pleasing odor to the LORD.
NRSVCE.10: And what is left of the grain offering shall be for Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the offerings by fire to the LORD.
NRSVCE.11: No grain offering that you bring to the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you must not turn any leaven or honey into smoke as an offering by fire to the LORD.
NRSVCE.12: You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of choice products, but they shall not be offered on the altar for a pleasing odor.
NRSVCE.13: You shall not omit from your grain offerings the salt of the covenant with your God; with all your offerings you shall offer salt.
NRSVCE.14: If you bring a grain offering of first fruits to the LORD, you shall bring as the grain offering of your first fruits coarse new grain from fresh ears, parched with fire.
NRSVCE.15: You shall add oil to it and lay frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
NRSVCE.16: And the priest shall turn a token portion of it into smoke — some of the coarse grain and oil with all its frankincense; it is an offering by fire to the LORD.

NET.1: “‘When a person presents a grain offering to the LORD, his offering must consist of choice wheat flour, and he must pour olive oil on it and put frankincense on it.
NET.2: Then he must bring it to the sons of Aaron, the priests, and the priest must scoop out from there a handful of its choice wheat flour and some of its olive oil in addition to all of its frankincense, and the priest must offer its memorial portion up in smoke on the altar — it is a gift of a soothing aroma to the LORD.
NET.3: The remainder of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and to his sons — it is most holy from the gifts of the LORD.
NET.4: “‘When you present an offering of grain baked in an oven, it must be made of choice wheat flour baked into unleavened loaves mixed with olive oil or unleavened wafers smeared with olive oil.
NET.5: If your offering is a grain offering made on the griddle, it must be choice wheat flour mixed with olive oil, unleavened.
NET.6: Crumble it in pieces and pour olive oil on it — it is a grain offering.
NET.7: If your offering is a grain offering made in a pan, it must be made of choice wheat flour deep fried in olive oil.
NET.8: “‘You must bring the grain offering that must be made from these to the LORD. Present it to the priest, and he will bring it to the altar.
NET.9: Then the priest must take up from the grain offering its memorial portion and offer it up in smoke on the altar — it is a gift of a soothing aroma to the LORD.
NET.10: The remainder of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and to his sons — it is most holy from the gifts of the LORD.
NET.11: “‘No grain offering which you present to the LORD can be made with yeast, for you must not offer up in smoke any yeast or honey as a gift to the LORD.
NET.12: You can present them to the LORD as an offering of first fruit, but they must not go up to the altar for a soothing aroma.
NET.13: Moreover, you must season every one of your grain offerings with salt; you must not allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be missing from your grain offering — on every one of your grain offerings you must present salt.
NET.14: “‘If you present a grain offering of first ripe grain to the LORD, you must present your grain offering of first ripe grain as soft kernels roasted in fire — crushed bits of fresh grain.
NET.15: And you must put olive oil on it and set frankincense on it — it is a grain offering.
NET.16: Then the priest must offer its memorial portion up in smoke — some of its crushed bits, some of its olive oil, in addition to all of its frankincense — it is a gift to the LORD.
